body: Wells Fargo Bank, representing a commercial mortgage-backed securities trust, filed foreclosure lawsuits in multiple states in August 2026 over the portfolio backing a $1.28 billion loan to Workspace Property Trust, Bisnow reported on August 24, 2026. A suit filed in Hennepin County, Minnesota puts the unpaid principal at about $1.23 billion, and the lender says it is owed that balance plus interest, special servicer fees and attorney expenses. KeyBank National Association is the special servicer and attorney-in-fact for the lender, according to the new suits.

Workspace obtained the CMBS loan in 2018, backed by 146 office and industrial properties totaling nearly 10 million square feet across four states. The portfolio now includes 143 properties in Arizona, Florida, Minnesota and Pennsylvania and is valued at $1.24 billion, down from $1.63 billion at issuance, according to Morningstar Credit. Occupancy is about 75%, down from nearly 89% at origination and 81% in 2022.

The loan moved to special servicing in May 2023. It was scheduled to mature in July 2023 without extension options, but Workspace obtained a two-year extension that month; CEO Thomas Rizk told Bisnow in 2023 that existing investors had put significant new money into the company as part of the deal. Trigild was appointed receiver for the entire portfolio after Wells Fargo filed suit in Maricopa County, Arizona, in September 2025.
Workspace Property Trust declined to comment, and Wells Fargo and KeyBank did not respond to Bisnow by press time.

timeline.label: Workspace Property Trust obtains a $1.28B CMBS loan backed by 146 office and industrial properties in four states
The loan transfers to special servicing
Workspace obtains a two-year extension of the loan
Wells Fargo sues in Maricopa County, Arizona; Trigild is appointed receiver for the full portfolio
Wells Fargo files foreclosure suits in multiple states, including Hennepin County, Minnesota
